# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
#
#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
#      option, not an engine column).
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
#
# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen  [$4=dlen  $5=elen]
  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"dlen":${4:-0},"elen":${5:-0},"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256 192 32

# 2 + 3 + 4: qemu built-in present; fakeA discovered with its fields
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null) \
  || fail "list engines exited non-zero"
echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu64" || fail "built-in qemu64 not listed:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA not discovered:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "256" || fail "fakeA vlen (256) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "cycle-accurate" || fail "fakeA kind not shown:"$'\n'"$out"

# 4b. RVV hw params: XLEN/DLEN/ELEN columns; an engine that reports none
# (the qemu built-in) shows "-" for each.
for col in XLEN VLEN DLEN ELEN; do
  echo "$out" | head -1 | grep -qw "$col" \
    || fail "list engines: $col column header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
done
echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "192" \
  || fail "fakeA dlen (192) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "32" \
  || fail "fakeA elen (32) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -w "qemu64" | grep -q -- "-" \
  || fail "qemu64 row should show '-' for unreported params:"$'\n'"$out"

# 5. hot-plug: drop a SECOND engine, re-run (no rebuild), both appear
make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeB" "vsim:fakeB" 128
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA missing after hot-plug"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeB" \
  || fail "HOT-PLUG: fakeB not discovered without rebuild:"$'\n'"$out"

# 6. sidecar fallback: a binary with no --describe + a <bin>.json descriptor
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 3
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
{"id":"vsim:sidecar","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
SIDE
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:sidecar" \
  || fail "SIDECAR fallback failed (vsim:sidecar not listed):"$'\n'"$out"

# 7. (opportunistic) real default scan: if vsim is built, its sim_* binaries
# must self-describe and appear. Skipped when vsim has not been built.
if ls "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/"sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  out=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^vsim:" \
    || fail "default scan discovered no real vsim engine:"$'\n'"$out"
fi

ok "F2 engine registry + self-describe"

# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "vsim:f0" functional    fm

# The "expect a real run" cases (2a/2c) reach abs_elf, which requires an
# EXISTING file (a typo'd path fails with "ELF not found" before the engine
# spawns); contents are irrelevant -- the fake engine just echoes its args, and
# the arch check no-ops on a non-ELF. Error-path cases keep their bare typo'd
# name (they fail at resolution, before abs_elf).
DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"

# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle "$DUMMY"
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v1 "$DUMMY"
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for cycle
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle a.elf b.elf
# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
# 2i. the model is named `cycle`; the old `accurate` spelling is now unknown.
expect 2 "unknown model 'accurate'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode accurate dummy.elf
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# 3. real vsim (guarded): a cycle run prints ONLY the program's own output plus
# andesim's own "[andesim] N cycles" line -- vsim's startup banner and its
# verbose [info] log (including the raw "N cycles simulated" the driver lifts
# the count from) are hidden. Pinned to ax45mpv_premium + the vplat rt_c_hello
# fixture (UART + SimControl exit): a known-good pair that DOES exit standalone
# and prints, so every assertion is deterministic (matches f9's engine choice).
# A timeout means vsim hung -> skip (defensive), not a failure.
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium
SIM="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
if [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 90 "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "[skip] real cycle: vsim hung (timeout); cannot assert output format"
  else
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "real cycle: rt_c_hello exited rc=$rc (expected 0):"$'\n'"$out"
    echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' \
      || fail "real cycle: missing '[andesim] N cycles' result line:"$'\n'"$out"
    echo "$out" | grep -q 'hello' \
      || fail "real cycle: the program's own output was dropped:"$'\n'"$out"
    # vsim's banner + [info] log (incl. its raw "N cycles simulated") are hidden.
    for noise in 'cycles simulated' 'Copyright' '^\[info\]'; do
      if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$noise"; then
        fail "real cycle: vsim noise leaked (/$noise/ should be hidden):"$'\n'"$out"
      fi
    done
    echo "[ok] real cycle: clean output -- program stdout + '[andesim] N cycles'; banner/[info]/raw count hidden (rc=0)"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real cycle run: need built $SIM and $ELF"
fi

ok "F8 run --mode cycle"

#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.

TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"

  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

# Three layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): passthrough_argv fills the qemu `standalone`
#      invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) and appends the post-`--` engine args
#      verbatim -- including a `-gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. CLI error paths (no engine needed): missing --mode, unknown model,
#      missing ELF, an extra positional, and engine!=qemu each exit 2 with a
#      clear message.
#   3. real passthrough (needs built qemu + a fixture): launch
#      `run --mode fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::PORT -S`; the gdbstub port opens and
#      qemu halts at reset -- the done-when "port opens, halts, debugger
#      connects". exec_passthrough's exit-code propagation is already covered
#      by the F5 infra test (and observed here only indirectly).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: the argv-assembly contract carries the passthrough behavior
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (passthrough_argv) failed"

# assert `$BIN run ...` exits with $1 and its combined output matches regex $2
expect_rc_match() {
  local want_rc="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want_rc for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "output missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2. CLI error paths (deterministic; no qemu)
expect_rc_match 2 'mode .* is required.*--help' "$BIN" run
expect_rc_match 2 "unknown model 'bogus'"    "$BIN" run --mode bogus p.elf
expect_rc_match 2 'missing ELF.*workload'     "$BIN" run --mode fast
expect_rc_match 2 'engine args go after --'  "$BIN" run --mode fast a.elf b.elf

  echo "[ok] real fast passthrough: qemu gdbstub halted + listening on :$PORT"
else

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --mode cycle` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "vsim:f0" functional    fm

# EXISTING file (a typo'd path fails with "ELF not found" before the engine
# spawns); contents are irrelevant -- the fake engine just echoes its args, and
# the arch check no-ops on a non-ELF. Error-path cases keep their bare typo'd
# name (they fail at resolution, before abs_elf).
DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"

# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle "$DUMMY"

expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf

expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v1 "$DUMMY"
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for cycle
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle a.elf b.elf
# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
# 2i. the model is named `cycle`; the old `accurate` spelling is now unknown.
expect 2 "unknown model 'accurate'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode accurate dummy.elf
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# andesim's own "[andesim] N cycles" line -- vsim's startup banner and its
# verbose [info] log (including the raw "N cycles simulated" the driver lifts

    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "real cycle: rt_c_hello exited rc=$rc (expected 0):"$'\n'"$out"
    echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' \
      || fail "real cycle: missing '[andesim] N cycles' result line:"$'\n'"$out"
    echo "$out" | grep -q 'hello' \
      || fail "real cycle: the program's own output was dropped:"$'\n'"$out"
    # vsim's banner + [info] log (incl. its raw "N cycles simulated") are hidden.
    for noise in 'cycles simulated' 'Copyright' '^\[info\]'; do
      if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$noise"; then
        fail "real cycle: vsim noise leaked (/$noise/ should be hidden):"$'\n'"$out"
      fi
    done
    echo "[ok] real cycle: clean output -- program stdout + '[andesim] N cycles'; banner/[info]/raw count hidden (rc=0)"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real cycle run: need built $SIM and $ELF"
fi

# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column.
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

# F1 contract: one ELF built against the vplat runtime (UART stdio +
# SimControl exit, NO libgloss_vh / semihosting) runs to completion on the
# cycle-accurate engine from reset: it prints via the modeled UART and
# terminates the simulation with exit code 0 via the SimControl write.
#
# This is the leg that is impossible with an -mvh build (vsim has no
# semihosting; see docs/archive/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
SIM="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Nonzero exit code must propagate through vsim too.
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_exit41.elf >/dev/null || fail "exit41 build failed"
timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: the SAME vplat_hello.elf runs the hybrid handoff:
#
#   andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
#     --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end
#
# QEMU1 fast-forwards the newlib boot, drains at say_hello; vsim resumes,
# runs printf -- the bytes go out the MODELED UART, cycle-accurately --
# and drains at vplat_roi_end. Asserts all three: the hello text (from the
# vsim leg), a window_cycles figure, and the PASS line.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -x "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "vsim not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?

printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing 'hello from vplat' (the vsim leg must service the UART): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[pc window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger pc ' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing PASS line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "F3 vplat_hello.elf on hybrid (printf measured on the vsim leg)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
SIM="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not built: $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local wd out rc
  wd=$(mktemp -d)
  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
  rm -rf "$wd"
  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
}

run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

ok "F4 vplat_file.elf HTIF file io parity (fast + cycle)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andesim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andesim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andesim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
# (grep without -q: early-exit + pipefail turns a MATCH into SIGPIPE failure)
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep ' T _start' >/dev/null \
  || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T _write' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T m_trap_entry' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andesim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landesim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"
